facts.Alabama: The Wright brothers ran a flying school near Montgomery, Alabama, in 1910.
facts.Alaska: Denali in Alaska is the tallest mountain in North America, at 20,310 feet.
facts.Arizona: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is about 277 miles long and more than a mile deep.
facts.Arkansas: At Crater of Diamonds State Park in Arkansas, visitors can keep any diamonds they find.
facts.California: Giant sequoia trees in California can live for more than 3,000 years.
facts.Colorado: Mesa Verde in Colorado protects cliff homes built by Ancestral Puebloans about 800 years ago.
facts.Connecticut: The Connecticut River is the longest river in New England, at about 410 miles.
facts.Delaware: Delaware was the first state to approve the U.S. Constitution, on December 7, 1787.
facts.Florida: Rockets and space shuttles have launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
facts.Georgia: Coca-Cola was invented in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1886.
facts.Hawaii: Measured from the sea floor, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller than Mount Everest.
facts.Idaho: Shoshone Falls in Idaho is taller than Niagara Falls.
facts.Illinois: Chicago dyes its river bright green every St. Patrick's Day.
facts.Indiana: The Indianapolis 500, a famous car race, is held in Indiana every May.
facts.Iowa: The baseball field from the movie "Field of Dreams" is real, and you can visit it in Iowa.
facts.Kansas: A monument near Lebanon, Kansas, marks the center of the 48 contiguous states.
facts.Kentucky: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky is the longest known cave system in the world.
facts.Louisiana: Jazz music got its start in New Orleans, Louisiana.
facts.Maine: Maine is the only state that borders just one other state: New Hampshire.
facts.Maryland: "The Star-Spangled Banner" was written after a battle at Fort McHenry in Baltimore, Maryland.
facts.Massachusetts: Basketball was invented in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1891.
facts.Michigan: Michigan touches four of the five Great Lakes.
facts.Minnesota: Minnesota is the Land of 10,000 Lakes, and it actually has even more than that.
facts.Mississippi: The name Mississippi comes from an Ojibwe word meaning "great river."
facts.Missouri: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis, Missouri, is 630 feet tall, the tallest arch in the world.
facts.Montana: Montana's Glacier National Park joins Canada's Waterton Lakes to form an International Peace Park.
facts.Nebraska: Chimney Rock in Nebraska was a famous landmark for pioneers on the Oregon Trail.
facts.Nevada: Great Basin National Park in Nevada has bristlecone pine trees that are thousands of years old.
facts.New Hampshire: Mount Washington in New Hampshire once recorded a wind gust of 231 miles per hour.
facts.New Jersey: The first organized baseball game is said to have been played in Hoboken, New Jersey, in 1846.
facts.New Mexico: Bats stream out of Carlsbad Caverns in New Mexico at dusk, and the cave has a huge room called the Big Room.
facts.New York: The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France, stands in New York Harbor.
facts.North Carolina: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.
facts.North Dakota: Theodore Roosevelt National Park in North Dakota is home to wild bison and prairie dogs.
facts.Ohio: Ohio's state flag is the only one in the country that is not a rectangle.
facts.Oklahoma: Oklahoma's state song is "Oklahoma!" from the famous musical.
facts.Oregon: Crater Lake in Oregon is the deepest lake in the United States, at 1,943 feet.
facts.Pennsylvania: The Liberty Bell is on display in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
facts.Rhode Island: Rhode Island is the smallest U.S. state by area, at about 1,200 square miles.
facts.South Carolina: South Carolina's official state beverage is milk.
facts.South Dakota: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota shows four U.S. presidents carved into granite.
facts.Tennessee: Nashville, Tennessee, is nicknamed Music City and is home to the Grand Ole Opry.
facts.Texas: Mission Control for NASA spaceflights is at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas.
facts.Utah: The Great Salt Lake in Utah is saltier than the ocean.
facts.Vermont: Vermont makes more maple syrup than any other state.
facts.Virginia: Eight U.S. presidents were born in Virginia.
facts.Washington: Mount Rainier in Washington is an active volcano covered in glaciers.
facts.West Virginia: The New River Gorge Bridge in West Virginia is one of the longest steel arch bridges in the world.
facts.Wisconsin: Wisconsin is nicknamed "America's Dairyland" and is famous for its cheese.
facts.Wyoming: Yellowstone, mostly in Wyoming, became America's first national park in 1872.
